correctness.rationale: The arc-minus-chord defect has a local cubic formula det(gamma-prime,gamma-double-prime)^2/(24 speed^3). Near each axial point, the curve has normal profile 1-|t|^p/p, yielding an exactly computed variance lattice cell. A tangent-Hölder chord bound gives the summable tail for p<3/2; the borderline d^{-1} curvature singularity gives eight half-axis logarithms totaling h^2 log(n)/12; integrable curvature permits Riemann-sum convergence for p>3/2. The phase multiset follows exactly from axial angles k*pi/2 and step 2*pi/n. An independently formulated numerical implementation passed 44 finite tests. No finite experiment substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: A natural intrinsic-volume approximation error for the exact radial angular polygon family has a sharp change in exponent at p=3/2, an explicit logarithmic leading constant, and a three-residue-class phase law below the threshold, distinct at least near p=1. These data sharpen qualitative convergence and distinguish cumulative curvature cost from the known maximum Hausdorff gap; they inform numerical geometric approximation under finite angular sampling rather than just restating a textbook convergence fact.
